messages.content: When will be sunset in Beijing today?

function.name: calculate_sunrise
function.description: Calculate the time of sunrise for a specific date and location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which sunrise time needs to be calculated.

date.description: The date for which sunrise time needs to be calculated in YYYY-MM-DD format. If not provided, current date is considered. Default: 1998-12-03

format.description: Format in which the time should be returned. If not provided, default format 'HH:MM' is considered.

message.content: I’m sorry—I don’t have a function that gives me the sunset time. I can only calculate sunrise times.
message.reasoning:
We need to call the function calculate_sunrise but we want sunset. The function name is calculate_sunrise; maybe it can also compute sunset if we specify something? But the function signature only has location, date, format. It says "Calculate the time of sunrise". So it's for sunrise only. We cannot get sunset with this function. We might respond that we can't provide sunset. Or we could approximate using sunrise + daylight length? But no data.

Thus we should say we don't have function for sunset.
